I'd like to discuss the first point from your post - making old stuff newer.

I have an IBM NetVista 6568-TBG computer with Windows 98 SE. I made it "newer" by completely patching the system (for example, adding USB support, UPnP, integrated ZIP support etc) and installing KernelEx (for modern browsers and Office 2007 compatibility pack for Office XP). It's now a perfectly usable work and productivity machine which serves all my purposes.

If something can be patched up or updated to the maximum without too much altering, I do that (instead of using something newer that fits the device less). For example, Windows XP can be installed on my IBM computer, but it's sluggish in comparison to Windows 98 running on that machine, so I took the 98 and "pimped it". The same with my PDA: it uses Windows Mobile 2003 SE, but thanks to amazing support from the modders, it can use systems up to the very late builds of Windows Mobile 6.5.3... but I preferred to take the 2003SE and update/patch it as far as I can, without destroying the look and feel of the OS.
